statutes.content: Summary of the official section, not a quotation of invented subsections. W.S. 1-21-201 applies to civil cases in circuit court when the amount claimed, exclusive of costs, does not exceed $6,000. The procedure for those cases is W.S. 1-21-201 through 1-21-205. The Department of Revenue may consolidate certain tax-collection claims under the same procedure, subject to dollar limits stated in the section. The statute does not exclude interest from the cap, and it does not create subsections on evidence rules, attorneys, or counterclaims.

Summary of the official section. A case starts when the state, a governmental entity, a person, or an organization appears in circuit court and signs an affidavit. The affidavit recites the defendant's full address, the nature of the claim, the amount due, and that demand was made and payment refused. The remedy is cumulative, so a claimant may instead use another available procedure. A party may appear in person or through an authorized employee, with or without a lawyer. If a lawyer appears, the other side is entitled to a continuance to obtain a lawyer. The circuit judge dockets the case. The filing fee is set by Small Claims Rule 3 at $10, plus any sheriff or process-server charge. It is not a sliding fee.

Summary of the official section, as amended effective July 1, 2021. The court files the affidavit and has the summons served as otherwise provided by law. If the defendant resides in Wyoming, the court may serve by certified mail to the defendant's address in the state, return receipt requested. Service by that mail is complete when the circuit judge receives the receipt signed by the defendant or the defendant's agent. Venue also follows W.S. 1-5-104(b) and W.S. 1-5-105 through 1-5-109. Small Claims Rule 4, effective December 1, 2021, allows suit in the county where the defendant has an address or where the claim, or some part of it, arose. Rule 1 says these court rules supersede conflicting statutes.

Summary of the official section, as amended effective July 1, 2021. The appearance date in the summons is not more than 20 days and not less than 12 days after service. Before July 1, 2021 the window was 3 to 12 days. The Judicial Branch small-claims page still describes that older window. For cases filed on or after the effective date, the statute controls. When the judge sets the date, the plaintiff is told to appear with the books, papers, and witnesses needed to prove the claim. This section is the appearance rule. It is not a hearing-and-burden statute.

Summary of the official section. At the hearing the plaintiff, the defendant, and their witnesses may offer evidence. No formal pleading other than the claim and notice is necessary, and the hearing is informal. No prejudgment attachment or garnishment may issue. After judgment, execution, including garnishment in aid of execution, may issue as it does in other circuit-court cases. This section is not the appeal statute.

Summary of circuit-court civil jurisdiction. Each circuit court has exclusive original civil jurisdiction for an action whose prayer does not exceed $50,000, exclusive of court costs, and for small claims under W.S. 1-21-201 through 1-21-205. Forcible entry and detainer, the eviction case, is a separate circuit proceeding under W.S. 1-21-1001 and following. A money claim over $6,000 and through $50,000 leaves the small-claims track and stays in circuit court. It does not go to district court merely because it exceeds $6,000.

Summary of comparative fault. W.S. 1-1-109 applies to wrongful death and to injury to person or property caused by fault. Fault includes negligence and other conduct the section lists. Contributory fault does not bar recovery when the claimant's fault is not more than 50 percent of the total fault of all actors. Damages are then reduced in proportion to the claimant's fault. Each defendant is liable only for that defendant's proportion of the total fault. This section is not a general measure-of-damages statute for contract or deposit cases.

Summary of small-claims venue. W.S. 1-5-104(b) provides that a small-claims proceeding under W.S. 1-21-201 through 1-21-205 may be brought in the county where the cause of action, or some part of it, arose. W.S. 1-5-102 is a different rule, for property that lies in more than one county. It is not the general small-claims venue statute. Small Claims Rule 4 also allows suit where the defendant has an address.

Summary of selected limitation periods. A written contract, agreement, or promise must be sued on within 10 years. A contract not in writing, and a liability created by statute other than a forfeiture or penalty, must be sued on within 8 years. An action for trespass to real property, for taking or injuring personal property, for fraud, or for an injury to the plaintiff's rights not arising on contract and not otherwise listed, must be brought within 4 years. Assault and battery, other than sexual assault, is 1 year. The period depends on the claim. There is no single 4-year period for both written and oral contracts.

Summary of the residential-deposit statute. After termination, the owner may apply a deposit to accrued rent, damage beyond reasonable wear and tear, cleaning back to the condition at the start of the rental, and other costs the contract allows. The balance, any prepaid rent, and a written itemization of deductions must be delivered or mailed without interest within 30 days after termination or within 15 days after the renter's new mailing address, whichever is later. If the unit is damaged, that period is extended by 30 days. The renter must, within 30 days of termination, tell the owner where payment and notice may be sent. A utilities deposit identified separately follows the different timeline in subsection (b). If the owner unreasonably fails to comply with subsection (a) or (b), the renter may recover the full deposit and court costs. If the owner prevails and the court finds the renter acted unreasonably in bringing the action, the owner may be awarded court costs. The statute does not add a treble penalty.

Summary of owner duties. W.S. 1-21-1202 requires an owner to maintain a residential rental unit in a safe and sanitary condition fit for human habitation, with operational electrical, heating, and plumbing and hot and cold running water, unless the parties agree otherwise in a signed writing or the unit is a seasonal rental not intended to have those amenities. The article does not apply to conditions that do not materially affect physical health or safety. W.S. 1-21-1203 requires a renter who is current on payments to give written notice of a health or safety condition and the repair requested. That notice is served by certified mail or in the manner specified by W.S. 1-21-1003. The owner then starts the repair or disputes the claim in writing. Withholding rent is not the remedy those sections describe. An order restoring possession is a forcible entry and detainer case under W.S. 1-21-1001, not a small-claims affidavit.

court_rules.source_title: Rules and Forms Governing Small Claims Cases
court_rules.content: Summary of Rule 1. These rules govern procedure in small claims cases in circuit courts. Statutes governing small claims that conflict with these rules are superseded.

court_rules.source_title: Rules and Forms Governing Small Claims Cases
court_rules.content: Summary of Rule 3. The fee for filing a small claims action in circuit court is $10. Service fees charged by a sheriff or process server are separate.

court_rules.source_title: Rules and Forms Governing Small Claims Cases
court_rules.content: Summary of Rule 4, effective December 1, 2021. A defendant in a small claims action may be sued in the county where the defendant has an address, or where the cause of action or some part of it arose.

court_rules.source_title: Rules and Forms Governing Small Claims Cases
court_rules.content: Summary of Rule 5. No answer and no responsive pleading is required in a small claims action.

court_rules.source_title: Rules and Forms Governing Small Claims Cases
court_rules.content: Summary of Rule 6. Strict rules of evidence do not apply. Irrelevant, immaterial, or unduly repetitious evidence shall be excluded. The court may receive the type of evidence reasonably prudent persons rely on in the conduct of their serious affairs. Hearsay that is probative, trustworthy, and credible may be received. The Wyoming Rules of Evidence are not the governing evidence code on this docket.

court_rules.source_title: Rules and Forms Governing Small Claims Cases
court_rules.content: Summary of Rule 7. An appeal of a small claims action to district court is processed under the Wyoming Rules of Appellate Procedure, and only on questions of law, not for a review of the sufficiency of the evidence. The rule cites Johnson v. Statewide Collections, Inc., 778 P.2d 93 (Wyo. 1989). W.R.A.P. 2.01 requires the notice of appeal to be filed with the clerk of the trial court within 30 days from entry of the appealable order. The appeal is not a trial de novo, and the deadline is not 10 days.

judicial_guides.content: Application note for this simulation, not an official bench guide. The user writes both sides, so the hearing rehearses that user's theory. It does not predict the other party's testimony. The real case starts with a sworn Small Claims Affidavit, a $10 filing fee, service, and an appearance 12 to 20 days after service. There is no jury. If the plaintiff does not appear, the Judicial Branch says the case is dismissed. If the defendant does not appear, the plaintiff is sworn and a default for the affidavit amount plus costs is the usual result. The court paper is a Judgment and Order, not findings of fact and conclusions of law. One circuit judge hears the case.

Application note, not an official elements checklist. Money claims that fit this docket include a debt the affidavit describes as justly due after a refused demand, unpaid work under $6,000, proven property damage, and a residential deposit under W.S. 1-21-1208. A lockout or a demand to be put back in possession is a forcible entry and detainer case. A repair order is not a small-claims money judgment. A freelance invoice is a contract claim. W.S. 27-4-104 is the wage-payment statute for an employee, and an employee may also use the Department of Workforce Services wage claim. Comparative fault under W.S. 1-1-109 is the fault rule for injury to person or property. It is not the measure of contract damages.

Application note on the hearing the Judicial Branch describes. There is no jury. The plaintiff goes first and must explain why the amount is due, using papers, photos, or witnesses. The defendant then tells the other side. Bring copies for the court and the other party. The judge may decide at the hearing or take the case under advisement and mail the decision. A subpoena for a witness is requested from the clerk. The Judicial Branch says the subpoena must be served at least five days before trial.
